Assertions.Name: P2

Assertions.Name: P3

Assertions.Statement: For k>=3 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}): if q_k(P/2)=1 then the least period of the forcing word q_k=y_{k-1} OR y_{k-2} is exactly P.
Assertions.Name: TF

Assertions.Statement: If j>=1 and eps_j=1 (least period of y_j is twice that of its forcing word) then y_j(P_j/2)=1.
Assertions.Name: TG

Assertions.Statement: For k>=3, if some parent j in {k-1,k-2} attains P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}) and has eps_j=1, then Q_k=P.
Assertions.Name: TH

Assertions.Statement: For all k>=3 the least period of the forcing word equals max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}); no OR of two parent diagonals ever has a period smaller than both.
Assertions.Name: H7

Assertions.Statement: If H7 holds for all k>=3 then the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (H7 implies H4).
Assertions.Name: TI

Assertions.Statement: Exact least diagonal periods, forcing periods and parities certified through offset 64 (largest period 2^27) by an independent big-integer implementation that reproduces all 52 v05 period-word hashes and agrees with a direct lattice evolution for t<=4096.
Assertions.Name: F5

Assertions.Statement: Every diagonal is 1 at its half period: y_j(P_j/2)=1 for all j>=1 (would close the open case of H7 through TF at t=0).
Assertions.Name: H14

Assertions.Statement: Cascade lemma: for k>=4 and P=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), if y_j(P/2)=1 for some 2<=j<=k-1 then Q_k=P.
Assertions.Name: TJ

Assertions.Statement: For every k>=3, Q_k=max(P_{k-1},P_{k-2}), and the least diagonal periods are nondecreasing (induction on k using TJ, TG, TA).
Assertions.Name: TK

Assertions.Statement: For every k>=3, P_k = P_{k-1}*(1+eps_k): the least period repeats or doubles, never otherwise; and it doubles infinitely often.
Assertions.Name: TL

Assertions.Statement: For k>=4, if eps_{k-1}=1 then eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 (doubling at k decided by the parity of the grandparent diagonal).
Assertions.Name: H15

Assertions.Statement: eps_k = ones_{k-2} mod 2 for every k>=4, with no doubling assumption on k-1.
Assertions.Name: H16

Assertions.Statement: After a doubling at k-1 (k>=4), eps_k equals the parity of the number of ones of y_{k-2} over its least period.
Assertions.Name: TM

Assertions.Statement: For k>=5 the least diagonal period never doubles three times in a row; hence log2 P_k <= log2 P_k0 + ceil(2(k-k0)/3).
Assertions.Name: TN

Assertions.Statement: Finite discrepancy: |2 S(N) - N| <= 3 sqrt(N) for all 16 <= N <= 2^20, S(N) the number of ones among c(0..N-1).
Assertions.Name: H9

Assertions.Statement: Finite run bound: every maximal constant center run [T,V] with 1 <= T and V < 2^20 - 1 has length <= 2 log2(T+1) + 4.
Assertions.Name: H13

Assertions.Statement: For every period 1 <= p <= 2^17 and every onset T <= 917498, some t >= T has c(t) != c(t+p) (2^20 center bits; independent reproduction of E2).
Assertions.Name: F6

Assertions.Statement: Every plateau of the doubling sequence (maximal run of eps_k=0, k>=3) has length at most 7.
Assertions.Name: H18

Assertions.Statement: If every plateau has length at most L, then log2 P_k >= 2 + floor((k-3)/(L+1)) for all k>=3; a plateau bound forces exponential growth of the diagonal periods.
Assertions.Name: TP

Assertions.Statement: Exact diagonal periods certified through offset 72 (largest period 2^31); all 64 E10 period-word hashes reproduced; new diagonals agree with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
Assertions.Name: F7

Assertions.Statement: For k>=3: if eps_k=1 the diagonal has an even number of ones per period; if eps_k=0 that parity equals the parity of the number of ones of q_k at odd positions.
Assertions.Name: TO

Assertions.Statement: eps_k is a function of (eps_{k-1}, eps_{k-2}, o_{k-1}, o_{k-2}) for every k>=5, where o_j is the parity of the number of ones of y_j per period.
Assertions.Name: H19

Assertions.Statement: The center is eventually p-periodic iff some agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) is infinite; so a finite bound on agreement runs for every p implies P1.
Assertions.Name: TQ

Assertions.Statement: On the first 2^20 center bits, every agreement run c(t)=c(t+p) for 1<=p<=4096 has length at most 44.
Assertions.Name: H21

Assertions.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k(t)=x(-t+k,t) is eventually periodic, with least eventual period a power of two dividing 2^k.
Assertions.Name: TR

Assertions.Statement: Exact least eventual periods and onsets of the left-edge diagonals certified for k<=72 (largest period 2^3, latest onset 100); agrees with a direct lattice for t<=4096.
Assertions.Name: F8

Assertions.Statement: The left edge grows at most half as fast as the right: log2(left-edge period of w_k) <= log2(P_k)/2 for every k>=1.
Assertions.Name: H22

Assertions.Statement: Every left-edge diagonal w_k has least eventual period at most 8.
Assertions.Name: H23

Assertions.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=600; reproduces loop 9 for k<=72 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
Assertions.Name: F9

Assertions.Statement: The left-edge front moves at 5/4: |onset_k/k - 5/4| <= 0.02 for every 1000 <= k <= 5000.
Assertions.Name: H24

Assertions.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=5000; reproduces loop 10 for k<=600 and a direct lattice for t<=1600.
Assertions.Name: F10

Assertions.Statement: Some left-edge diagonal with k < 20000 has least eventual period 32.
Assertions.Name: H25

Assertions.Statement: Exact left-edge periods and onsets certified for k<=19999; for every 20<=k<=19999 the onset exceeds k, so the center c(t)=w_t(t) is read before its left-edge diagonal settles.
Assertions.Name: F11

Assertions.Statement: If the center p-agrees at t and t+1 then column -1 p-agrees at t when c(t)=1, and column -1 p-agrees at t iff column 1 does when c(t)=0: under center agreement, column -1 is column 1 read at the center's zero-times.
Assertions.Name: TS

Assertions.Statement: For every onset 1<=T<=10 and every nonconstant primitive word a of period p<=4, the left cone and the inverse rule alone exclude a p-periodic center of word a from onset T: no column-1 window is compatible once L reaches some L<=4T+4p+8.
Assertions.Name: H26

Assertions.Statement: Left-cone relaxation table for every onset T<=10 and every primitive word of period <=4: the number of column-1 windows (on the zero-times) compatible with a periodic center and the single-seed cone, for L<=4T+4p+8, with the first L that has none; the true (c,r) windows pass the same checker.
Assertions.Name: F12

Assertions.Statement: For every onset T, every p>=2 and every nonconstant word a of least period p, the left-cone relaxation (periodic center word a from T, free column 1, inverse rule, cone of T0) is unsatisfiable at some finite L(T,a).
Assertions.Name: B5

Assertions.Statement: For L>=T the left-cone relaxation is in bijection with rows R at time T on positions -T+1..-1 such that the Rule 30 evolution of the left half from R, with the center prescribed as boundary x(0,t)=c'(t), satisfies x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at every one-time t<=T+L-1; column 1 is determined, and count(T,a,L)<=2^(T-1).
Assertions.Name: TU

Assertions.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word a of period p<=6 and every onset 2<=T<=T_max(a) that exact enumeration completes (live-set cap 2^23), the left cone excludes the periodic center with L(T,a)<=4T+4p+8.
Assertions.Name: H27

Assertions.Statement: Exclusion lengths L(T,a) of the left-cone relaxation for every primitive word of period <=6, onsets from 2 up to the enumeration limit per word (largest completed onset 144); vectorised search validated against the loop 13 table and an independent SAT encoding of TU.
Assertions.Name: F13

Assertions.Statement: For t>=T and j<=t-T, x(-1,t) = x(-j-1,t-j) XOR XOR_{i=1..j}(x(-i,t-i) OR x(-i+1,t-i)); in the relaxation the leading term is a free row bit for t<=2T-2, the edge for t=2T-1 and 0 for t>=2T, so every one-time constraint from time 2T on is a parity of ORs along a light ray with no free-row term.
Assertions.Name: TV

Assertions.Statement: For every primitive nonconstant word of period 7 or 8 and every onset T>=8 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^23), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64: the relaxation dies by time 2T+64, independently of T.
Assertions.Name: H28

Assertions.Statement: Exclusion lengths, death times and violated cone cells of the left-cone relaxation for all 366 primitive words of periods 7 and 8 at onsets [8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 160, 192] up to the enumeration limit (largest completed 192); death-cell histograms recorded.
Assertions.Name: F14

Assertions.Statement: For the single-zero words a=0 1^(p-1), p in [8, 10, 12, 16], and every onset T>=32 that exact enumeration completes (cap 2^25), the left-cone exclusion excess L(T,a)-T is at most 64.
Assertions.Name: H29

Assertions.Statement: Exclusion lengths, excess and death cells of the left-cone relaxation for the single-zero words of periods [8, 10, 12, 16] at onsets from 32 to the enumeration limit (largest completed 384), with the excess fitted against T and log2 T.
Assertions.Name: F15

Assertions.Statement: In the forward form, the one-time constraints at T<=t<=2T-2 fix the row bit at position -(t-T+1) as a function of the bits to its right and leave the bits at zero-time positions free: exactly 2^Z rows survive to 2T-2 (Z = zero-times in [T,2T-2]), and every constraint at t>=2T-1 is a Boolean function of those Z bits.
Assertions.Name: TW

Assertions.Statement: For every T>=2 and every nonconstant periodic word, each of the 2^Z rows of TW violates x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at some one-time t>=2T-1.
Assertions.Name: B6

Assertions.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period p<=5 and every onset 4<=T<=18, the largest algebraic degree over the Z free bits among the one-time constraints applied before death is at least Z-1: the kill is maximally nonlinear, so B6 is not linear algebra over GF(2).
Assertions.Name: H30

Assertions.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period <=5 and onset 4..18: Z, the TW count check, and for each one-time constraint after 2T-2 until death its algebraic degree over the Z free bits, live counts before and after, and whether it was constant on the live set.
Assertions.Name: F16

Assertions.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 and every onset 4<=T<=46, a cone cell violated by every surviving window exists at the death step, and its time t*(T) is non-decreasing in T with steps 0 or 1.
Assertions.Name: H31

Assertions.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 at onsets 4..46: the death window, survivors, the violated cone cells with counts, the common killing cells, whether the edge cell is among them, and t*(T).
Assertions.Name: F17

Assertions.Statement: B6 for the period-2 words 01 and 10: for every onset T>=2, each TW row for a 2-periodic center violates a one-time constraint at or after 2T-1 (equivalently, the Rule 30 center is not eventually 2-periodic).
Assertions.Name: B7

Assertions.Statement: B6 for every nonconstant word of least period p>=3.
Assertions.Name: B8

Assertions.Statement: The dyadic wall is exact for period 2 past onset 36: for a=01 and every onset 47<=T<=50 the left-cone relaxation dies at window exactly 64, and for a=10 at exactly 65.
Assertions.Name: H32

Assertions.Statement: L(T) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 2<=T<=50 (loop 18 data plus onsets 2, 3 and 47..50 computed here with cap 2^26), with survivors at the death step.
Assertions.Name: F18

Assertions.Statement: The 64-wall is exactly the TW boundary phenomenon: for the words 011,101,110 (pinned window 66) and 0111,1011,1101,1110 (pinned window 64) the death window keeps its pinned value from the first pinned onset through T=63 and exceeds it at T=64,65,66; for 01 and 10 at onsets 51 and 52 it stays at 64 and 65.
Assertions.Name: H33

Assertions.Statement: Structure of the 64-wall for the word 01 at onsets 37..46: forced cells on the death ray (none in the cone interior), tie classes by column (columns 1-3 tied, 4-5 partly, 6 onward untied), GF(2) independence of the 33 one-time functions over all rows for T<=18; and the L(T) table of H33 for period-3 and period-4 words at onsets 44..66.
Assertions.Name: F19

Assertions.Statement: With every settled left-edge diagonal imposed on the periodic-center relaxation (exact values, or periodicity only), the death window exceeds the settled frontier by at most 8 (exact) or 16 (periodic only) for the words 01 and 10 at every onset 8<=T<=160 the search completes: the clash with the settled zone is local.
Assertions.Name: H34

Assertions.Statement: Settled-zone relaxation table for the words 01 and 10, exact and periodicity-only modes, onsets 8..160: frontier, death window, excess, peak live set, failing columns; the true lattice satisfies every imposed constraint to time 400.
Assertions.Name: F20

Assessments.Name: F14

Assessments.Name: H29

Assessments.Name: F15

Assessments.Name: TW
Assessments.Statement: In the forward form, the one-time constraints at T<=t<=2T-2 fix the row bit at position -(t-T+1) as a function of the bits to its right and leave the bits at zero-time positions free: exactly 2^Z rows survive to 2T-2 (Z = zero-times in [T,2T-2]), and every constraint at t>=2T-1 is a Boolean function of those Z bits.

Assessments.Name: B6
Assessments.Statement: For every T>=2 and every nonconstant periodic word, each of the 2^Z rows of TW violates x(-1,t)=NOT c'(t+1) at some one-time t>=2T-1.

Assessments.Name: H30
Assessments.Statement: For every nonconstant primitive word of period p<=5 and every onset 4<=T<=18, the largest algebraic degree over the Z free bits among the one-time constraints applied before death is at least Z-1: the kill is maximally nonlinear, so B6 is not linear algebra over GF(2).

Assessments.Name: F16

Assessments.Name: H31

Assessments.Name: F17
Assessments.Statement: For the words 01 and 10 at onsets 4..46: the death window, survivors, the violated cone cells with counts, the common killing cells, whether the edge cell is among them, and t*(T).

Assessments.Name: B7

Assessments.Name: B8

Assessments.Name: H32

Assessments.Name: H33

Assessments.Name: F19
